How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow
all speakers to address the City Council.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the online public
comment form at Public Comment. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00
P.M. on the meeting day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for
their consideration, but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after
4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

   City Council Special Meeting Agenda
  Monday, April 21, 2025

•  CALL TO ORDER
•  ROLL CALL: Mayor Menchaca, Vice Mayor Chan, Council Members Ding, Herrera Avila,
  Wu

  1. PUBLIC COMMENT

  2. FISCAL YEAR 2025-2026 BUDGET STUDY SESSION FOR PROPOSED CITY
  OPERATING BUDGET AND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM

  The preliminary Operating Budget and Capital Improvement Program (CIP) for Fiscal
  Year 2025-2026 are submitted to the City Council for initial review, facilitating a
  detailed examination of the proposed figures and seeking further guidance. Total
  proposed city-wide operating revenues total $89.4 million, with corresponding
  expenditures totaling $86.5 million. The General Fund comprises revenues of $57.7
  million and expenditures of $56.8 million, resulting in a positive net change in fund
  balance of $933,000. The city-wide expenditure figures include $2.7 million for new
  capital improvement projects.

  Not a project as defined in Section 15378 of the state CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and discuss the Fiscal Year 2025-
  2026 proposed operating budget and Capital Improvement Program; and provide
  direction to staff, as appropriate.

  3. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, May 6, 2025, at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be
  available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF APRIL 21, 2025
  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Menchaca called the special meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
  5:32 P.M. on Monday, April 21, 2025, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South
  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, Jorge Herrera Avila, John Wu, Vice Mayor
  Eric Chan, and Mayor Denise Menchaca
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney
  Martin Koczanowicz, Community Services Director
  Rebecca Perez, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Fire Chief
  Steven Wallace; Human Resources/Risk Management
  Director Edward Macias, Finance Director William
  Kaholokula, Acting Community Development Director

I  Samantha Tewasart, Acting Public Works Director John
  Gonzalez, Police Captain Edwin Brock, and Assistant City
  Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  1. PUBLIC COMMENT - None.

  2. FISCAL YEAR 2025-2026 BUDGET STUDY SESSION FOR PROPOSED CITY
  OPERATING BUDGET AND CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM

  Finance Director Kaholokula and Assistant Finance Director Linda Tang made the
  presentation.

  Discussion included general fund projected surplus; non-inclusion of labor negotiation
  and Cost of Living Adjustments (COLA) adjustments in salary figures; funding Other
  Post Employment Benefits (OPEB) contributions and Capital Improvement Program
  (CIP) expenditures with excess reserve funds; Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT)
  projections; explanation of transfers in and out; Proposition A exchange options;
  uncertainty in the current political climate; licenses and permits revenue decreases
  based on historical trend and conservative projections; sales tax details for Measure

I  SG, state sales tax, and state-mandated Public Safety Augmentation Plan (PSAF);
  potential for the City to capture an additional quarter per cent sales tax via ballot
  measure when the County's Measure H sunsets; farmers market funding would be
  allocated separately when more detail is available; enhancing City events; one-time
  expenditures and grant applications; and grant funding for Smith Park facilities.

  3.  ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 6:49 P.M.
